correctness.rationale: For p,q>=3, Farber-Hanbury maturity yields the natural equivariant H1(F2)->H1(K_p,q squared) isomorphism and A_p tensor A_q in two particle positions, splitting equally in swap signs. The cubical deleted-product model has chains only in degrees 0,1,2; explicit fixed-cell traces under (sigma,pi) and particle exchange, including negative orientation of swapped edge×edge cells, give chi2_unswapped=(f_p^2-3f_p+1)(f_q^2-3f_q+1) and chi2_swapped=-(2t_p-1)(2t_q-1). Standard Sym²A=1+A+T, wedge²A=W character identities split H2 into (Wp⊠Tq)^+ +(Tp⊠Wq)^+ +(Wp⊠Wq)^- +(Tp⊠Tq)^- (T3=0). Independence of the part permutation groups makes the four external-tensor irreducibles distinct. H0 trivial and H_i=0 for i>2. Independent finite parameter and character-identity tests passed; general theorem follows from exact equivariant Euler–Poincare and mature-graph theorem.
